key_insight: Controlling presentation biases improves answer selection, while deliberately inducing majority pressure exposes decision instability as a reliability signal.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a test-time way to aggregate heterogeneous LLM answers without validation data or prior knowledge of model strengths.
method: Present one style-normalized reasoning trace per distinct answer to reduce style and majority biases.
Place each aggregating agent’s initial choice in the minority to probe decision instability.
Use the resulting reliability signal to guide answer aggregation.
evidence_signal: Across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks and four heterogeneous LLM combinations, the framework reports higher average accuracy and better token efficiency than competing non-oracle aggregators, plus accuracy gains for multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents.
watch_item: Style normalization must preserve reasoning content; the abstract does not establish whether gains generalize beyond mathematical reasoning.
paper_title: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
